who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), executor T4 of track 7b, int-1112
what: A launched run binds a function's first call from a record keyed by its describe key, which holds content and never place, so one record serves every machine. The bytes it binds hold names of files (`file!()`, a panic's location, the span tables positions are read from), and a registry crate's are under `$CARGO_HOME`: a key of the describe alone would serve one machine's names on another. The revision driver could not say a launched run is the built program either: it read no exit status, never ran the file `blaze build` makes, and counted no spans.
cost: a launched run's correctness rested on review; no case caught a key that missed the names
cause: a store key was reused for an output with one more input than the value it was made for (rule 21)
class: a key carried over from one value to a derived value whose bytes read more than the first
prevention: each record's key is built from its own value's inputs: the bind key is the describe key, the naming, the policy and the program's symbols; a case that changes only the input left out shows in the program's output
fix: naming_of hashes the names of the root files of the home and every crate it loads; a_naming_moves_with_a_root_files_name_and_with_nothing_else holds it (control: the dependencies left out). The revision cases a_launched_run_*_prints_what_the_built_program_prints hold a run to the built file's stdout, stderr and status; the six-dependency one moves $CARGO_HOME under a second home and prints the directory hashbrown's panic names.
